response:
I can grant some nuance without pretending I don't have a view. Some roles and some people genuinely do better together — mentoring, early-career learning, certain kinds of creative collision. That doesn't make the two approaches equally good for most knowledge work, and it doesn't make "it depends on the individual" a fair summary of company-wide mandates.

When leadership ignores their own productivity and retention data and forces everyone back anyway, control and real-estate sunk costs are usually doing more work than evidence. I'm not going to sand that down into "both sides." If you disagree, I'd rather hear the actual counterargument.
